input:
Write a bash script that rotates numbered log files.

Starting files in /home/eval/logs (nothing else is in that directory):
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log ---
line c
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.1 ---
line b
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.2 ---
line a
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.3 ---
line 0
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.old ---
manual backup
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log ---
w2
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log.1 ---
w1
--- end ---

Define a shell function `rotate LOGFILE KEEP` implementing classic numbered rotation:
- `LOGFILE.N` becomes `LOGFILE.N+1` for every existing N, highest first, so nothing is overwritten.
- Afterwards no numbered file above KEEP may remain (delete any that would end up numbered higher than KEEP).
- `LOGFILE` itself becomes `LOGFILE.1`, and a new empty `LOGFILE` is created.
- Files that are not exactly `LOGFILE` or `LOGFILE.<number>` (for example `app.log.old`) must not be touched.

Then call it twice: `rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3` and `rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2`. Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

rotate() {
    local logfile=$1
    local keep=$((10#$2))
    local candidate suffix n i j max_index tmp_n tmp_entry
    local -a entries=() numbers=()

    for candidate in "$logfile".*; do
        [[ -e "$candidate" || -L "$candidate" ]] || continue
        suffix=${candidate:${#logfile}+1}
        [[ $suffix =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue

        n=$((10#$suffix))
        entries+=("$candidate")
        numbers+=("$n")
    done

    # Sort numbered files by number, highest first, so moves cannot overwrite.
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#numbers[@]}; i++)); do
        max_index=$i
        for ((j = i + 1; j < ${#numbers[@]}; j++)); do
            if (( numbers[j] > numbers[max_index] )); then
                max_index=$j
            fi
        done
        if (( max_index != i )); then
            tmp_n=${numbers[i]}
            numbers[i]=${numbers[max_index]}
            numbers[max_index]=$tmp_n

            tmp_entry=${entries[i]}
            entries[i]=${entries[max_index]}
            entries[max_index]=$tmp_entry
        fi
    done

    for ((i = 0; i < ${#numbers[@]}; i++)); do
        n=${numbers[i]}
        if (( n >= keep )); then
            rm -f -- "${entries[i]}"
        else
            mv -- "${entries[i]}" "$logfile.$((n + 1))"
        fi
    done

    if [[ -e "$logfile" || -L "$logfile" ]]; then
        mv -- "$logfile" "$logfile.1"
    fi

    if (( keep < 1 )); then
        rm -f -- "$logfile.1"
    fi
    : > "$logfile"
}

rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3
rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2
exit 0
```
